content.prompt: Show that each function is increasing for its entire domain.

answer.short: $y'=\dfrac32\sqrt{x}>0$ for $x>0$. Also, $y(0)=0<x^{3/2}$ for every $x>0$, so the function is increasing on $[0,\infty)$.
answer.worked:
The domain is $x\geq0$.

$$\begin{aligned}y'&=\frac32x^{1/2}\\&=\frac32\sqrt{x}>0\qquad(x>0)\end{aligned}$$

Hence the function is increasing for $x>0$.

At the endpoint, $y(0)=0<x^{3/2}$ for every $x>0$. Therefore the function is increasing on its entire domain $[0,\infty)$.

answer.short: $y'=\dfrac{1}{4x^{3/4}}>0$ for $x>0$. Also, $y(0)=0<x^{1/4}$ for every $x>0$, so the function is increasing on $[0,\infty)$.
answer.worked:
The domain is $x\geq0$.

$$\begin{aligned}y'&=\frac14x^{-3/4}\\&=\frac{1}{4x^{3/4}}>0\qquad(x>0)\end{aligned}$$

Hence the function is increasing for $x>0$.

At the endpoint, $y(0)=0<x^{1/4}$ for every $x>0$. Therefore the function is increasing on its entire domain $[0,\infty)$, although its derivative is undefined at $x=0$.
